name: Casan Buidhe

attributes.attribute: form taken to frighten travelers at a ford
a magical being who destroyed the wizard

sources: McKay, John G. More West Highland Tales. Vol. 2. Scottish Anthropological and Folklore Society. Edinburgh: Oliver and Boyd, 1969, 461.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Casan Buidhe was a Scottish folkloric figure. He was a famous wizard. His names included Yellow Legs and Weaver of the Yellow Legs. He preyed on travelers who tried to cross rivers. He shifted shape into a large stag. The stag panicked those who stood mid-ford. They dropped their treasures to flee, or they drowned in fright. The wizard then took their wealth. At last a smith faced him. A smith in this tale is a magical being. The smith destroyed the wizard.

okr.objective: Casan Buidhe is a shape-shifting wizard who robs travelers, killed by a smith.
key_results: Scottish tradition calls him a famous wizard.
He shifts into a large stag at a river ford.
He takes the wealth of travelers he terrifies.
A smith, a magical being, confronts and destroys him.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
